title: A Protocol for Detecting and Scavenging Gas-phase Free Radicals in Mainstream Cigarette Smoke
protocol: Dissolve pycnogenol and grape seed extract in 95% ethanol.
Dissolve lycopene in acetone.
Stir activated carbon with the antioxidant solution for approximately 12 hours under anaerobic conditions.
Filter and dry the mixture under vacuum.
Coat 0.4 mg of antioxidants onto 10 mg of activated carbon.
Cut a conventional acetate filter into two pieces.
Insert the coated plant antioxidants between the two cut pieces of the filter.
Wrap the assembled parts with tape to form a filter-antioxidant-filter sandwich.
Attach the combined filter to cigarette rods containing tobacco.
Make a control filter in the same manner but without adding any antioxidant.
Unpack research cigarettes and keep them in a constant humidity environment (20 °C, 60% relative humidity) for a minimum of 2 days using a saturated NaBr solution.
Set up a single-port smoking device with a water aspirator or GAST DOA-P104-BN Vacuum Pump/Air Compressor connected to the spin-trapping assembly through a T-junction.
Adjust the valve between the pump and vent to set gas flow at ~2.2 SCFH = 17.5 mL/s as checked by flow meter.
Smoke research cigarettes under conditions of puff volume of 35 mL for a duration of 2 seconds, repeated every 60 seconds.

Perform smoking simulation with spin trapping system to collect gas-phase free radicals by passing the MCS through a Cambridge filter pad and then introducing it into the spin trapping solution (0.05 M PBN in benzene, 2.0 mL).
Readjust the bubbled trapping solution to its initial volume of 2.0 mL after collection with the same benzene.
Transfer an aliquot from the trapping solution into a ~250 mm long, 3 mm ID glass tube sealed at one end for analysis.
Deoxygenate the trapping solution using a freeze-pump-thaw procedure.
Freeze the solution under liquid nitrogen.
Apply vacuum to remove dissolved gases.
Thaw the solution under an argon atmosphere.
Repeat freezing, applying vacuum, and thawing two more times for a total of three cycles.
Flame-seal the tube under vacuum after the final cycle.
Use the deoxygenated solution in further ESR measurements.
Record X-Band ESR spectra on a Bruker EMX spectrometer at 9.34 GHz.
Set center field to 3312.5G and scan width to 80G.
Use modulation amplitude of 0.5G, time constant of 82 microseconds, and scan time of 40 seconds for measurements.
Accumulate up to 25 scans when necessary to improve signal-to-noise ratio.
Quantify the concentration of trapping adduct by integrating its first-derivative ESR spectrum.
Subtract broad singlet background from initial spectrum before integration.
Employ a spin trap technique to capture gas-phase free radicals from cigarette smoke.
Use a spin-trap solution of 0.05 M PBN to collect the free radicals.
Add a liquid nitrogen (LN2) trap between the Cambridge filter and the spin trap solution to remove moisture.
Quickly freeze and capture water on the inner wall of the glass tube using LN2.
Improve ESR signals and achieve highly reproducible results.
Determine the amount of trapped free radicals using a reference sample.
